Modern.brandNameRationale: Single word. Evening names the time of day the customer actually uses the product. The brand sits on the moment, not the plant. Plain, mature, and built around the hour rather than the substance.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern cannabis has moved from emerging-market hype toward design-led brands. The customer is design-literate, often older than the early-legalization stereotype, and looking for brands that talk about cannabis the way a wine brand talks about wine.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Houseplant (houseplant.com) holds the modern design-led peer position. Dosist (dosist.com) sits in the wellness-leaning tier. Eaze (eaze.com) does the consumer marketplace middle. Cann (drinkcann.com) holds the beverage-led peer. We sit closest to Houseplant in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A cannabis brand that talks about the time of day, not the substance.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Uses cannabis occasionally and considers it part of an evening, not an identity. Already buys design-led adult goods. Will pay a premium for product that looks at home on a kitchen counter.

dos: Talk about the evening, the room, the hour
Show the product on a real coffee table

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. EVENING in a soft modern grotesk, all caps, seven letters with wide kerning. A small geometric mark, a single thin crescent suggesting an evening moon, used as the favicon and the package seal.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for product specs
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the technical product data. The regular carries the brand.

customSections.title: Where it lives

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two distinctive words joined by an ampersand. Halls suggests a heritage house with long corridors and old wood. Bough is the older English word for a branch of a tree, with botanical associations. The pair reads as a heritage botanical apothecary that has been operating quietly for over a century.
Luxury.story: Halls & Bough was founded as a botanical apothecary at the turn of the last century. The current generation operates in the modernized cannabis space while keeping the apothecary tradition. The catalog is small. The clients are mostly older, mostly inherited, mostly long-standing.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end cannabis has been moving toward larger brands and bigger marketing. There's a parallel market for small heritage-feeling brands that operate like botanical apothecaries from another century. Quiet packaging, considered selection, decades-long relationships. The customer is paying for the apothecary, not the substance.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Beboe (beboe.com) holds the design-led luxury peer position. Lord Jones (lordjones.com) sits in the institutional luxury tier. Saint Jane (saintjanebeauty.com) does the wellness-luxury middle. We sit quieter and more heritage in tone than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small heritage botanical apothecary with a quiet cannabis catalog.

targetAudience.primary: Wealthy, often inherited. Uses cannabis occasionally. Values the apothecary tradition. Pays for considered packaging and discreet delivery.

dos: Address the client by surname in writing
Name the botanical, the source, the maker

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn ampersand becomes the apothecary's hallmark, used on the bottle labels, the apothecary book, and the wax seal of every paper letter.

colorPalette.name: Apothecary Green
colorPalette.meaning: Old apothecary cabinet, the botanical wall.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure allocation portal
typography.rationale: A high contrast classical serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles the few digital surfaces.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No mass distribution. No celebrity endorsements. No social media presence. No press tour. No publicly listed clients.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Herb is the oldest, plainest word for what cannabis actually is: a plant. The brand sits on the botanical truth, before the slang and the marketing. Plain, slightly old-fashioned, and immediately legible.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most cannabis brands have elaborate names suggesting wellness, luxury, or counterculture. There's an opening for one that strips it back to the most basic word for the plant.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most cannabis brands fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some Japanese herbal traditions and certain Chinese herbal-medicine aesthetics.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A cannabis brand named after the plant.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who use cannabis occasionally and want it sold the way other botanical products are sold. They want the product, the dose, the receipt.

dos: Show the product, the strain, the price

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. HERB in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps, four letters with generous space. No icon. The packaging, the website, and the receipt all carry the wordmark and nothing else.

typography.rationale: One face. The packaging, the website, and the receipt all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Three words. Trellis is the agricultural structure that cannabis is grown on. The brand sits on the literal infrastructure of cultivation, not the consumer-facing language. & Co. closes it as a real, established firm. Distinctive without being overstyled.
Corporate.industrySummary: B2B cannabis (cultivation, distribution, licensing services) is a real category serving licensed dispensaries, brand operators, and regulated wholesalers. Buyers want partners with operational discipline and clean compliance documentation.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Curaleaf (curaleaf.com) holds the institutional MSO peer position. Cresco Labs (crescolabs.com) sits at the same tier. Trulieve (trulieve.com) is the southern peer. We sit smaller and more focused on the cultivation-and-distribution side.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Cannabis cultivation and wholesale distribution for licensed operators.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Licensed dispensaries and brand operators want supply partners with operational discipline, clean compliance, and consistent quality. The category incumbents are uneven. We sit on the more disciplined side.

targetAudience.primary: Dispensary owners, brand operators, and wholesale buyers at licensed cannabis companies. They sign multi-year supply contracts.

dos: Lead with the cultivation operation and compliance documentation
Show case studies with retail-partner economics
Speak to the buyer, not the end consumer
donts: Promote individual SKUs on consumer social

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. Good Couch names the actual destination of most cannabis use: the couch, after dinner, with one person. The brand puts the universal experience in the brand position. Warm, slightly self-deprecating, and refreshingly honest about what the product is for.
Creative.manifesto: Most cannabis brands sell wellness, luxury, or counterculture. We made Good Couch because the truth about cannabis is that most of it ends with someone on a couch, lights low, eating something they didn't plan to eat. The brand is for the small private hour. The lights are dim. The phone is face-down. The couch is good.
Creative.industrySummary: Cannabis branding has been split between wellness theatre and youth-culture posturing. There's room for a brand that's warm, honest, sticker-friendly, and serious about the actual relaxed experience the customer is paying for.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Houseplant (houseplant.com) does design-led restraint. Cann (drinkcann.com) holds the beverage middle. Old Pal (oldpal.com) sits in the friend-with-weed peer position. We sit warmer and more honest about the couch.
Creative.positioningStatement: A cannabis brand for the small couch hour after dinner.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Uses cannabis occasionally, almost always at home, almost always on a couch. Buys the brand because the marketing made them feel seen rather than upsold.

dos: Talk about the couch, the snack, the movie
donts: Photograph models in linen at sunset

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the O of GOOD stylized as a small filled circle, like a lamp from above. Standalone lamp-O icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every package.
